TITLE: Feeling the heat yet, Andy? Burnham faces questions over flip-flopping on Brexit, tax and immigration as he launches Makerfield by-election campaign TODAY
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-22 09:47 (updated 09:53)
AUTHOR: James Tapsfield
SOURCE: Daily Mail

KEY:
- Andy Burnham formally launches Makerfield by-election campaign today (Friday 22 May)
- Faces questions over flip-flopping on Brexit, tax, immigration

POSITIONS NOW:
- Brexit: BACKED OFF pledge to rejoin EU — "deeply unhelpful in an area that heavily endorsed Brexit"
- Fiscal rules: allies say will stick to Reeves' fiscal rules (after markets took fright at previous hints they could be torn up)
- Immigration: backs Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's tough immigration crackdown
- To Manchester Evening News today: "stronger grip" is needed on UK's borders

PAST POLICIES FLOATED:
- 50p top rate of tax increase
- Praised Gordon Brown's "disastrous 10p tax rate"
- Mass nationalisations

CONTEXT:
- Lack of definition of mayor's approach "has come to the fore as the Makerfield by-election ramps up"
- Sir Keir Starmer said yesterday he would be campaigning in Makerfield
- Spokesman for mayor: "Anyone who wants to embrace Andy's campaign message is welcome on the campaign"
- Burnham takes on Reform UK's Robert Kenyon (local plumber who contested seat in 2024)
